units.title: Brackwater junction: finished (allegedly).
units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Morning report. The Brackwater junction roadworks are finished. The temporary lights are gone, loaded onto a flatbed at 06:10 while I watched like a man at a funeral. Two weeks late and somehow worse: the new right-turn lane fits exactly one car, so a van sticks out into the main road. The dip is dry again. Congratulations to everyone involved, including the pump.

units.author: sb_bins
units.text: Collected again this morning, on the correct day, by the correct lorry, and my box was returned to the correct house. Two successes in one week. I don't quite know what to do with myself. I've written to the council to say thank you, which will confuse them more than any complaint I've ever sent. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear Mr Garrick, thank you for being so honest, and please do not feel sorry. You are a very kind young man to offer a mat. I must tell you, though, that I hear the steps at three in the afternoon as well, when I come back from the post office, and I don't think you run at three in the afternoon. Irena, 7C

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Something nice, since Bev asked and won't stop asking. My grandson passed his driving test yesterday, first time, in the pouring rain, on a route that takes in half of the old number 9. I drove that route for twenty-two years. I told him where the examiners like to put the hidden stop sign by the depot. He says that's cheating. It's knowledge.

units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: Late to this, rig was out of signal. Break food on the eastbound: a gas station burrito that I can only describe as warm, a pickle the size of my forearm, and a slice of my wife's banana bread that I'm rationing like a prospector. No satsuma. I've let the board down.

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Don't get used to it, Bernard. In Weyhaven they collected ours on time this week as well, and then left every lid in the middle of the road, so the wind took six of them into the car park and one onto the bonnet of a Kerrow Estates van, which I won't pretend I minded.

units.title: Parcels for the Holm crew: what to put in?
units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: As promised, a practical thread. The Lisle Women's Institute will assemble parcels for the crew as soon as an address is confirmed, and we would welcome suggestions. So far we have socks, a scarf, fruit cake, shortbread from Gilliver, a box of paperbacks from Tollinby and a stack of newspapers. Please keep suggestions sensible: no alcohol, nothing that needs a fridge, and no lucky charms.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: 'Feedback, positive' should be framed. Kennel equivalent: the owner who rang at two to ask whether her dog 'had made any friends'. He has. He's made friends with a very old basset called Lord Henry and they sleep back to back in the corridor that Duke won't walk down. So that's two dogs who don't mind it, at least.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: From the water: Gilliver shore lights steady on both crossings last night, and the night before. Not a flicker on the approach. The deck floods are still on the genset anyway, because nobody in their right mind is going to take them off now. Pint owed to Garvey, logged.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: From a parent's point of view: hand warmers, the ones you snap; lip balm; a pack of cards; good tea bags, not the cheap ones; and a torch with spare batteries, because you can never have too many and somebody always borrows yours. Also 26 children's cards with glitter trees, which I'm told are non-negotiable.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Update for anyone still wondering: I claimed the goodwill payment yesterday under the new eight-hour rule, using Bernard's sums and the oven clock. It took four minutes on the phone and the man was very nice. The freezer survived. The fish fingers did not, but that was the youngest, not the power.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: The school bus came back through the dip this afternoon and the youngest was very disappointed, because the ridge road has a farm with a llama on it and the dip has nothing but a lot of brown water marks. I've promised her the llama at the weekend. Mill Lane's open again too, according to the bus driver.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Davey, my mum in Brackwater has a birch down across her back garden from the rain, roots and all, lying on the shed. Not urgent, it's not going anywhere. Is that the sort of job you mean? She'll pay in cash and cake. I'll message you her number.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Good luck, Ada. You took every line we ever threw you on that pier, in every weather, and you never once dropped one. The surgery's lucky. We'll give you a blast on the horn coming round the point on your first evening off, if the new attendant doesn't mind.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Good luck, Ada. I mean that. Whatever either of us saw, you always said yours exactly as you saw it and never made it bigger, and that's more than most people on these boards manage. Come for a drink at the Lisle Arms on Saturday. I'm buying. No talking about slipways.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: A gentle note on the parcels. If they are being organised, please do it through Mrs Hale's thread and the Women's Institute, and please don't send anyone down to the Gilliver slipway at night to try to hand things to a boat. The harbourmaster has enough to deal with this week. Thank you all for the kindness.

units.title: Chapter 4 sent (I am now a beanbag)
units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: Chapter 4 draft sent to my supervisor at 02:00, with a covering email that I reread nine times and still contains the phrase 'please find attached the thing'. I'm going to sleep in the beanbag in the lab common room. The corridor lights can do what they like. Thank you to everyone on here who kept me company through it, especially the satsuma.

units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: She came in to celebrate and bought one cake bar and one sparkling water. I put a candle in the cake bar. We don't sell candles; it was the emergency one from under the till. She blew it out. The forecourt light flickered when she did, which she said was 'a sign'. I said it was the forecourt light.

units.title: The man on the forecourt (short update)
units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: Short update for the people who asked. The man at the edge of the forecourt light, the one with the different coat, hasn't been back for three nights. The local man waiting for his lift is still there most nights, in the same coat as always. I asked him whether he'd seen the other one. He said 'which other one'. I sold him some gum.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Gloves. Proper ones, the thick rigger gloves, not the knitted kind, because they'll be going through a pair every couple of days on that job. Spare chain files as well if anyone has a few, a 4.8 mm fits most saws. I'll drop a box off at the W.I. hall if someone tells me where it is.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Exactly the sort of job I mean. Birch on a shed, roots up, dead easy. I'll come Saturday with the small saw and the trailer and take the lot away for logs. Cash and cake is my favourite rate. Tell her not to try and move it herself in the meantime.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Ferry side: every sailing on time today, both ways. The 07:40 left at 07:40. I checked my watch against the terminal clock. I'm told this has happened before, but nobody alive can remember it. If the roadworks are finished and the ferries are on time, I can only assume something terrible is about to happen to the buses.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Evening run. New right-turn lane at Brackwater confirmed rubbish: I sat in it with the van's back end in the main road while a tractor went round me with about an inch to spare. Somebody at the council drew it on a computer and never drove it. I'll be writing in. Bernard, lend me your phone menu technique.

units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: I run the flower shop on Market Row, so I can't send flowers that would last, but I can make up little bags of dried lavender to go in with the socks. They smell of summer and they keep things fresh in a damp bag. I'll do one for each person on the crew if somebody tells me how many.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Clear tonight, first time in three days, and cold coming down off the hill already. Lights came on out there at dusk the same as ever. You can see them sharp as anything tonight. Aunt Maud has her lamp lit and says she's sure they can see it, and I've not the heart to tell her nine kilometres.

units.title: Logs floating off Gilliver: why?
units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: The Coastguard says there's cut timber floating between Gilliver and the Holm. Cut timber. From where? There's one island in the Sound being felled right now. Are they dumping the logs in the sea at night so nobody sees how many trees were really there? Just asking. Nobody on the mainland has been offered a single load, the Trade Journal says so.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: So: an ice plant isolated at the board, a coolbox on 12 V and a wheelhouse fridge that its owner says was off. That's three 'offs'. One of them is probably wrong, because the hum is real and it's mains. I'd bet on the Marigold's owner misremembering. But I'd only bet a small amount.

units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Pebble went out tonight! For the first time in over a week, for about three minutes, just after the streetlight came on properly and stayed on. She sat on the back step looking at the dark garden, then came in and sat on my feet for an hour. So I think it was the streetlight going off with the cuts. Thank you, everyone.

units.title: First dry night: owls back on the edge of town
units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Headphones on. First dry evening in three days, so I stood at the end of the allotments by the cemetery wall for twenty minutes after work. Two tawnies calling back and forth, one left and close, one right and far, and between them the ring road like a long breath. The ground is still dripping everywhere. Raw file attached, eighteen minutes.

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Thank you, all of you. This is the best thread we've had on this board in a year, and I've been secretary for six. Roses in November, a driving test, six herons, a honey cake and a lift that works. I've printed it out (perks of the job) and pinned it on the lobby board next to the fire inspection notice. Bev, DCRA

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: I'll take that bet for the same small amount. I've asked the Marigold's owner twice and he's sure, because he cleared it out in August and left the door propped. So that's that. It's still a pump somewhere. Probably. I'm going to stop posting about it before it becomes my whole personality.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Good file. Down here the harbour's gone very quiet after the rain: the burns are running into it brown and slow, and with the hydrophone over the wall all I can hear is fresh water layering over the salt, a sort of low fizz. No pumps. Not a single one, of course, tonight of all nights.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: That's lovely news. Ours went straight back out once our streetlight was fixed too, so I think you've got your answer. Three minutes is a start. By next week she'll be bringing you presents again, which is less lovely, but it's how you know they're back to normal.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Went out for a look at slack water before dark. Got close to one, three metres or so, birch. Clean cut both ends, saw marks plain as day, no bark missing to speak of. Could be anybody's, mind. The old mill at Brackwater stacks birch right by the burn and the burn was over its banks. I've told Quill where it is.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: The cards are finished. Twenty-six of them, and the teacher says she'll 'find out' about sending them, with Mrs Hale's parcels if that happens. My eldest's says: 'Thank you for cutting the trees. Please don't get cold. Our dog is called Biscuit.' I didn't have the heart to correct the spelling of biscuit.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: Tawnies, aye, and they'll be loud all week now the rain's off and they've lost half their perches. You can record them perfectly well from the edge of town, as she's just shown, without anyone setting foot in my woods after dark. The car park closes at dusk. I'll be checking.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Lovely spacing on that. The near owl has a hard reflection off the cemetery wall about 40 ms after each call, which is a good reminder for everyone of how much a single wall can do to localisation. The far one is clean. That's the one I'd put on the sleep playlist.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: It rained for three days, Gil. Trees fall in rivers. Rivers go in the sea. There's a sawmill on the Brackwater burn with half its yard in the water. A bloke in Gilliver who fishes for a living has already said so. Grow up and read the thread before you start one.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: I checked the bin store on 8 after my shift, at 21:50. The chiller is there, by the back wall. The plug is out and taped to the side, like Hassan said. I put my hand on the back: cold, no vibration. I listened for ten minutes with the door shut. Nothing. So there is a chiller on 8, and it is switched off. I was wrong and also right. Sorry for spelling.

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Thank you, Benedikt, for checking properly and for putting the door back on the latch. The council now say the bulky collection is next Tuesday. I will believe it when I see the lorry. If anyone wants a large drinks chiller that doesn't work, it is free, you carry it. H

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Thank you for checking; that's the cleanest test anyone could have done. So: the right machine in the right room, in the wrong state. I withdraw it as an explanation for the recording. I still think the sound is structure-borne and mechanical. I no longer know what machine.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Recorded, for the thread. 1. Chiller on 8: present, unplugged, cold. 2. Treadmill on 10: present, in use roughly 05:00 to 06:00. 3. Reports with a time attached: 23. 4. Of those, 19 fall between 23:30 and 03:00. Neither item 1 nor item 2 matches item 4. I note this. I am not counting.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Garrick, thank you for coming forward; that took more than most people here have offered. On timing: you run from about 05:00. Of the 23 timed reports, 19 are between half eleven and three in the morning, two are around five, and two are in daylight. The two at five you may well explain. Possibly not the rest.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Something nice, as requested. The left lift has now operated for 72 consecutive hours without a fault. That is the longest run since I began keeping a note of it, which I admit I have. n=1 lift. I rode it to 9 tonight and it smelled only slightly.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Welcome back. That's all from me. Headphones on for your next one, whenever it is, and I'll lend you the binaural head again if you want it. Nobody owes a forum a reason for leaving a field early. We all go home when it's time to go home.

units.author: lh_crane_halvard
units.text: Clear and cold tonight, the first frost on the cab roof at midnight. Wind under four. You can see stars even over the city, and the ring road looks like it's been polished. Flask lid still leaks, cab 4417, I've taken your advice and drink from the side. Two lifts, both glass. Very careful. No questions.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: so the treadmill explains like two of them. that's two more than anything else has explained this whole month lol. garrick you're a legend and you've accidentally done more science than any of us. still doesn't explain irena's afternoons. still doesn't explain mine at 2am. but two.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: self-closer man coming thursday 9 to 3. I'm going to be there with a clipboard and a cup of tea for him, asking if a closer can open a door by itself. purely for my engineering education. if he says yes I'll be relieved. if he says no I'll be very polite about it.

units.author: lh_carer_vellmark
units.text: Thank you, everyone, for your kind replies; I read them on my break with a cup of tea and had a little cry in the laundry, which is where we go. Her daughter came in today to collect her things and asked me to thank 'the night ones'. The intercom is still quiet. The new resident in her room snores very loudly, which is somehow a comfort.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: 00:40 fox on camera 3, same limp. Logged as 'fox, known'. 01:30 patrolled east stack, nil found. 02:00 clear sky, cold, reefer row quiet. 02:50 a ship's crew walking back from the town, singing; nil of concern. 04:00 rolls. The fox has now appeared on four nights and I've given it a name in the log, which my supervisor says is not procedure.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: What's the fox called? I'm going to need to know, because my lad on the bike says he saw it by the north gate on his way back with the empty basket and I'd like to put a roll out for it. Not procedure either, I'm sure. Fresh batch of seeded rye tonight; yours is in the paper bag with the fox drawn on it.

units.title: Three weeks without the van
units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Patrol notes. It's been three weeks since the van at the edge of the car park lights, and nearly a week since the one A_road_regular and I both saw at the Brackwater junction. Neither has been back. Control asked me tonight if I missed it. I said no. Walked the whole perimeter twice anyway, slowly, with the big torch, and found two trolleys and a lost shoe.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Update from B corridor: A&E quiet tonight. Street lights on everywhere, no 'fell in the dark' from Gilliver all week, and the frost hasn't really started yet, so the trolleys are standing about looking bored. My mate's still off the forums and still humming. Orange crisps remain the only crisps. Back on the run.

units.title: Going on days
units.author: lh_taxi_halvard
units.text: news anyway, I'm going on days from next week, the firm's short of daytime drivers and my wife has been asking for nine years so I said yes before I could think about it, I'll miss the rank and the nurses and the drunks who sing, I won't miss the dark bits of the ring road where nobody's ever standing when you look twice, anyway I'll still read this on my lunch

units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: never saw it at our end of the shared yard, for what it's worth, and we've got cameras on every door. two trolleys and a shoe is a good night by our standards. we found a forklift battery in the canteen fridge once. nobody ever owned up. break's over

units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: I'll miss you on the rank, cab 4417, and so will the whole ward. You've driven me home more times than my own family has. Days will suit you. Your wife is a patient woman and she deserves dinner with you at a normal hour. I'll find another lift. Back to it.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Good man. Half the night shift I've known over the years went on days in the end and not one of them came back to nights, which tells you everything. The sun is apparently very nice. I'm told you can see the vending machines properly in it.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Good decision, clinically and otherwise. Nine years of nights is a long time for a body. Expect a fortnight of feeling jet-lagged in your own city, and get outside in the morning light as much as you can for the first week. And yes: the dark bits of the ring road will still be there. You just won't be in them at four.

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping, the nice kind: cab_4417 is going on days, and the board will be quieter for it. Daytime members are very welcome here too, whatever the name says. Lamp Hours is company on whatever shift you work. Good luck, and thank you for nine years of fares.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: There's a line in an old novel about a night watchman who retires and spends his first morning off simply standing in the market square, astonished by how many people there are. I hope your first day shift is a little like that. Thank you for all the stories.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: I'd add only this, as the one who misheard a name on the radio. I believe Dmitra's account completely. I also notice I've started leaving the shop lamp on when I lock up at night, which I never used to do. I don't think those two facts argue with each other. I think most of us are living with both.

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: Bus home. Frost here too. Every streetlight in town on this week since they fixed the substation. People still stand in their doorways at dusk out of habit, mind, a minute or two, looking down the street, then go in. Nobody talks about it. Kettle on.

units.title: Bus depot after the rain
units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: Hello loves, a depot report from Weyhaven since it's been a while, three nights of rain means three nights of mopping out the inspection pits, which fill up like paddling pools, and tonight they were finally dry so I sat on an upturned bucket with my flask and listened to the buses ticking as they cooled, which is the nicest sound in the world, and every bus was dark inside, every single one, which made me very happy

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: (Two out of twenty-three is a start, and more than my chair ever managed.) I'm drawing Garrick as a very muscular hamster in a wheel, affectionately, with a tiny towel. Irena's afternoons and Jordie's 2am are still blank spaces in the drawing. I've left them white on purpose.

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: something nice love, I came home just now and the sky over the docks was already going pale green at the edges and there was frost on every car in the car park like icing, and the stairwell lights were on, and Hassan's bread van was just pulling up, and I thought well, that's a good morning, that is

units.author: dc_10_garrick
units.text: Something nice, legends. Put a proper rubber mat under the treadmill this morning, two inches thick, cost me a session's pay. Ran on it at five as usual and my neighbour on 10 says it's like I'm not there. So that's maybe two of Tobin's twenty-three sorted, mate. The other twenty-one are yours.

units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: I'd add a small lamp, maybe, a battery one for a windowsill. Sorry, that's probably silly. They'll have plenty of lights out there, you can see them from here. I just thought one in a window might be nice, the way Maud keeps hers. Ignore me if it isn't the sort of thing that goes in a parcel.
